P levels vary widely (0, 30, 60, 120, 240, 480 mg P kg-1 soil) - mineral concentration responses differ substantially across P levels, especially for Fe and Zn.
Table 1 reports shoot tissue mineral data (blades and sheaths separately) at 56 DAP (vegetative stage), NOT grain data - do not confuse with grain mineral concentrations.
Grain mineral data (Zn, Fe) are reported in Figure 4 only - no tabular data available for grain Zn and Fe, only graphical.
Grain N and P concentrations are in Table 2 - these are grain quality data, not shoot data.
Grain Ca and amylose are in Figure 3 only - graphical, no tabular data.

Shoot N in Table 1 shows DECREASE at elevated CO2 (consistent with dilution hypothesis).

No variance data (SE, SD) are reported in tables - only means. LSD values are reported in Table 2 only (LSD p=0.05: N=1.0, P=0.3).
Harvest timing differs between CO2 treatments: 139 DAP for 700 ppm, 146 DAP for 350 ppm - different developmental timing could affect concentrations.
Table 1 values are described as 'pooled means of five replicates' with no variance reported per cell.
Zn in Table 1 is in mg kg-1 dwt (micronutrient), while P, Ca, N are in g kg-1 dwt - units differ within the same table.
Starch data in Table 1 is NOT a mineral element - do not extract for mineral meta-analysis.
The paper states critical P concentration was 1.8 g kg-1 for both CO2 levels - CO2 had no effect on foliar P concentration, which contradicts dilution for P specifically.

recon.extraction_guidance: 1. TISSUE TYPE: Separate extractions needed for shoot tissue (Table 1, blades vs sheaths) and grain tissue (Table 2, Figs 3b, 4). These represent different organs and developmental stages. 2. P LEVELS: Each of the 6 P levels should be treated as a separate data point or averaged across P levels if pooling - be explicit about which P level is used. The paper recommends moderate P as the most responsive. 3. VARIANCE: No SE/SD available for Table 1 or figures. Table 2 provides only a single LSD value applicable across all P levels. If variance is required, this paper can only contribute mean data. 4. Ca DIRECTION: Ca increases at elevated CO2 in both shoot and grain - extract as positive effect, not negative. 5. N and Zn DIRECTION: Both decrease at elevated CO2 in shoot and grain - extract as negative effects. 6. P in SHOOT: CO2 had no significant effect on foliar P concentration - extract as near-zero effect. 7. GRAIN vs SHOOT: For meta-analysis of grain mineral dilution, prioritize Table 2 (grain N, P) and Fig 4 (grain Zn, Fe) over shoot tissue data in Table 1. 8. PSEUDOREPLICATION WARNING: Only 1 chamber per CO2 level - statistical comparisons between CO2 treatments using pot-level variance are pseudoreplicated. Flag this limitation in extraction. 9. For Figure 4 (Zn, Fe in grain): values must be read from graph at each P level - consider averaging across P levels or selecting specific P levels for extraction. 10. Harvest dates differ between treatments (139 vs 146 DAP) - note this as a potential confound.
